subject: Temporary escrow for operator runbook & evidence access
messages:
From: Amanda Li <amanda.li@securehealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: SecureHealth Legal Ops <legalops@securehealth.com>, SecureHealth Infra <support@securehealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-18 09:12 PST
Subject: Request: temporary access to operator runbook + escrow-like evidence for on-prem POC

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the SecureHealth infra team is excited to move to a short pilot for the private (on-prem) deployment. Before we approve the POC we need two items from Redwood:

1) A timebound copy of the operator runbook and a minimal set of operational evidence (screenshot or snapshot of runbook procedures, list of required credentials and recovery steps) that our SREs can validate against our control matrix.
2) An escrow-like assurance or temporary holdback: we need a mechanism so SecureHealth Legal can verify we could operate the deployment independently (read-only access to runbook + a sealed-forensic snapshot and handback process) during the pilot window. This is scoped to the POC only (30 days) — not production.

Attached is our standard evidence checklist for POCs. Please confirm whether Redwood can provide a limited-runbook extract and agree to the sealed snapshot workflow. Also please indicate whether you require an NDA or any addendum to the Order Form for this access.

Best,
Amanda
Amanda Li
Head of Cloud Strategy, SecureHealth
--- Attachment: securehealth_poc_evidence_checklist.pdf (pdf)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amanda Li <amanda.li@securehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-18 11:03 PST
Subject: Re: Request: temporary access to operator runbook + escrow-like evidence for on-prem POC

Amanda —

Appreciate the clear ask and the checklist. Short answer: we can support a time-limited, read-only extract of the operator runbook plus a sealed forensic snapshot for the POC, with a narrow evidence package. We typically handle this via an MSA/Order Form annex (short addendum) that defines scope, retention, and handback procedures.

Proposed approach (high-level):
- Provide a redacted runbook extract (operational steps, no secrets) in read-only form for 30 days.
- Produce a sealed snapshot (tarball checksum + notarized statement) retained by Redwood; provide SecureHealth a one-time verification token and MD5/SHA hash for validation.
- Access window: POC start to POC end (we can align dates once you confirm).
- Legal: we will need a short annex (Order Form addendum) and a mutual attestation clause — Marissa, can you advise on wording?
- Ops: Karthik, are there any procedural blockers or internal constraints for producing the sealed snapshot?

I'll attach a sample runbook extract and an access matrix proposal for your review.

Thanks — Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head, Customer Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
--- Attachments: operator_runbook_sample.txt (text), access_matrix_proposal.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Amanda Li <amanda.li@securehealth.com>, SecureHealth Legal Ops <legalops@securehealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-18 14:26 PST
Subject: Re: Request: temporary access to operator runbook + escrow-like evidence for on-prem POC

Thanks Naomi — drafting guidance below and flagging a couple of redlines we need SecureHealth to consider. Amanda, copying for transparency.

Legal notes / requested redlines (summary):
- Limited-scope annex: 30-day POC access window; explicit statement that access is read-only and Redwood retains custody of any sealed snapshot.
- Non-production clause: Annex must explicitly state the POC is not a license to operate or modify the platform in production.
- Evidence handling: SecureHealth may verify the sealed snapshot via checksum and a one-time validation token; any additional forensic access requires a written request and a pre-defined escalation (we should keep this to emergency-only).
- IP and residuals: Redwood must preserve IP ownership of runbook content; SecureHealth may retain redacted copies for audit only, with deletion cert on handback.
- Liability cap carveout: Legal prefers no increase to overall liability; instead propose mutual indemnities limited to gross negligence or willful misconduct.

Amanda — attached is our first-pass redline to an MSA annex (redlines_MSA_20261118.pdf). If that works, we can produce a short Order Form addendum to tie dates and the POC order. Karthik — operationally, we will need a list of allowed verification activities and a contact for runbook access.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Amanda Li <amanda.li@securehealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-19 09:18 PST
Subject: Re: Request: temporary access to operator runbook + escrow-like evidence for on-prem POC

Quick ops note:
- We can produce the runbook extract and a sealed snapshot within 5 business days once dates are finalized and the annex is signed. The sealed snapshot process is: create sanitized snapshot -> compute SHA256 -> sign with platform key -> store in WORM storage -> provide verification token to customer.
- Limitations: we cannot provide privileged credentials or any live console access for the POC. All telemetry/log extracts will be synthetic examples or stripped of PII.
- Access model: read-only PDF (watermarked) + one-time verification procedure. We'll need a SecureHealth SRE point-of-contact and an SDN (service delivery number) to track the request.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Platform Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Request: temporary access to operator runbook + escrow-like evidence for on-prem POC

Amanda —

Thanks for the patience. Next steps proposed:
1) Amanda to confirm POC window (start/end dates) and nominate SRE contact.
2) SecureHealth to review the attached redlined annex (redlines_MSA_20261118.pdf) and confirm acceptance or provide a countermark by EOD 2026-11-23.
3) Upon agreement, Redwood will produce the runbook extract and sealed snapshot within 5 business days and provision read-only access for the 30-day window.
4) Delivery package will include: redacted runbook (PDF, watermarked), sealed snapshot checksum + notarized statement, and an access-handback deletion certificate template.

If these terms are acceptable, Marissa will prepare the short Order Form addendum and I'll coordinate the ops delivery.

Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head, Customer Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
